title: Survey of Different Large Language Model Architectures: Trends, Benchmarks, and Challenges
explain_beginner: This paper reviews how large language models, the AI systems behind chatbots and writing tools, have evolved and improved. These models use billions of interconnected components trained on massive amounts of text to understand and generate human language. Newer versions, called multimodal models, can also process images, audio, and video, enabling tasks like describing pictures or editing videos. The survey examines how different models compare and identifies remaining challenges, helping readers understand what these tools can and cannot do.
explain_business: Organizations evaluating LLM deployment should reference this technical comparison to move beyond marketing narratives toward objective capability assessment. The survey clarifies which models suit specific applications, from straightforward text tasks to complex multimodal requirements like video processing. Understanding architectural differences and identified limitations helps enterprises select appropriate solutions, anticipate integration challenges, and plan for evolving capabilities. This grounded analysis informs procurement, development prioritization, and realistic timeline expectations for AI initiatives.
explain_practitioner: This survey traces LLM architectural progression from foundational transformer-based designs through contemporary multimodal implementations. The authors systematically evaluate state-of-the-art models across technical characteristics, functional capabilities, and performance benchmarks rather than relying on vendor claims. The analysis covers model capacity scaling from billions to trillions of parameters, task versatility spanning text generation through code analysis, and the emerging MLLM category integrating vision and audio processing. The comparative framework identifies architectural trade-offs, performance limitations, and development trajectories to guide implementation decisions.
